<action type="say">
Here’s how to move forward with Northwest Federal Credit Union in the US:

1) Phone (fastest for a damaged card)
- Go to nwfcu.org in your browser.
- Scroll to the bottom and look for “Contact Us” or “Help” to find the main phone number and any card‑specific numbers (like Visa credit card support or a 24/7 card services line).
- When you call, say something like:
  “I need to report my personal credit card as damaged and request a replacement mailed to the address on file.”
- Ask them to:
  • Confirm the card will continue to work until the replacement arrives (or whether they’ll issue a new number).  
  • Confirm your mailing address and estimated delivery date.

2) Online banking / mobile app
- Log in to NWFCU online banking or the mobile app.
- Look for sections such as:
  • “Cards” / “Card Management” / “Card Services”  
  • “Messages” or “Secure Message Center”  
- If there’s a card management option, check for “Replace card,” “Report damaged card,” or similar.
- If you only see secure messaging, send a message stating:
  “My personal credit card is physically damaged. Please order a replacement card mailed to my address on file. I do NOT believe the card is lost or stolen.”

3) While you wait for the new card
- Avoid any transactions that might damage the chip/magstripe further (if it’s already unreliable, it may start failing more often).
- Be prepared to update any autopayments (subscriptions, bills) once the new card arrives if NWFCU issues a new card number/expiration date.

If you’d like, I can draft a short message you can paste into the secure message center or use as a script when you call NWFCU.</action>
